plan.title: Whole blood case vs control DE with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: 60 cases vs 60 controls in whole blood, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 121 samples incl. metadata), single batch, unpaired. The question has two parts: which genes differ (statistical significance) and which differences are large enough to matter (effect size). With 60 per group the knowledge base flags that count-based negative-binomial models (DESeq2/edgeR QLF) exaggerate false discovery in population cohorts of this size (R-0015), so the primary test is limma-voom with TMM normalization, a fixed-effects design explicit on reference level (control), and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test run in parallel as a robustness control against the same false-positive inflation. Genes are called by BH-adjusted p<0.05 (never raw p, never fold-change alone), but 'large enough to matter' is answered by a TREAT test against an explicit |log2FC| threshold (not a post-hoc filter on the point estimate) and by reporting effect size (moderated log2FC with its SE) alongside every adjusted p-value, sorted by effect size within the significant set — directly addressing the sample-size-induced problem that at n=60/group even trivial fold changes reach significance. QC precedes the model (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to catch structure or outliers before any test is fit. Downstream, camera (accounts for inter-gene correlation, appropriate at this sample size) and fgsea preranked on the moderated t-statistic characterize which coordinated biological programs (MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome) carry the signal, run on the full ranked gene list rather than a p-value-thresholded subset. A final report step consolidates DE table, effect-size ranked calls, enrichment, fit diagnostics, and a full reproducibility record.

Reproducibility record included: session info, package versions, any random seeds used, gene set collection version(s), annotation release used for ID mapping

Explicitly distinguishes 'genes that differ' (BH-significant) from 'differences large enough to matter' (TREAT-thresholded / effect-size-ranked subset), directly answering both halves of the research question
steps.context: Consolidates the DE calls (T1S2), effect-size shrinkage/ranking (T1S3), and pathway enrichment (T2S1) into one decision-ready report answering both parts of the research question: which genes differ, and which differences are large enough to matter.
constraints: Do not present exploratory enrichment signal as confirmed biology — state it as hypothesis-generating, per the method-dependence caveat
Report the TREAT threshold and BH cutoff as explicit, stated design choices, not silent defaults
caveats: At n=60/group, statistically significant does not imply biologically large — this is the central caveat the report must foreground, consistent with the effect-size-beside-p-value requirement

grounding.reason: No single rule covers report assembly as a step type in the knowledge check schema, but the constituent reporting rules (R-0085, R-0087, R-0089, R-0041, R-0051, R-0055, R-0105, R-0086) are all satisfied by the acceptance criteria above.
